commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	"""The NightJar web app: one server-rendered page plus a small JSON API.
2	
3	Run with:  uv run uvicorn nightjar.web:create_app --factory --reload
4	"""
5	
6	import os
7	from collections.abc import Callable
8	from datetime import UTC, datetime, time
9	from pathlib import Path
10	
11	from fastapi import FastAPI, Form, Request, UploadFile
12	from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse
13	from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
14	from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates
15	from pydantic import BaseModel
16	
17	from nightjar.coach import Coach, ask_coach, get_coach
18	from nightjar.coach.service import DEFAULT_TRACE_PATH
19	from nightjar.diary import Diary, local_input_to_aware, parse_csv
20	from nightjar.models import Night, User
21	from nightjar.nudge import next_nudge
22	from nightjar.search import search_nights
23	from nightjar.sleep_window import usual_bedtime
24	
25	HERE = Path(__file__).parent
26	Clock = Callable[[], datetime]
27	
28	
29	def system_clock() -> datetime:
30	    return datetime.now(UTC)
31	
32	
33	class CoachQuestion(BaseModel):
34	    question: str
35	
36	
37	def create_app(
38	    diary: Diary | None = None,
39	    coach: Coach | None = None,
40	    clock: Clock = system_clock,
41	    trace_path: Path = DEFAULT_TRACE_PATH,
42	) -> FastAPI:
43	    diary = diary or Diary(os.environ.get("NIGHTJAR_DB", "nightjar.db"))
44	    coach = coach or get_coach()
45	    templates = Jinja2Templates(directory=HERE / "templates")
46	    app = FastAPI(title="NightJar")
47	    app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=HERE / "static"), name="static")
48	
49	    def render(request: Request, status_code: int = 200, **extra) -> HTMLResponse:
50	        user, nights = diary.user(), diary.nights()
51	        context = {
52	            "user": user,
53	            "nights": nights,
54	            "usual_bedtime": usual_bedtime(nights),
55	            "nudge": next_nudge(user, nights, clock()),
56	            "imported": request.query_params.get("imported"),
57	            **extra,
58	        }
59	        return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "index.html", context, status_code=status_code)
60	
61	    @app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
62	    def home(request: Request):
63	        return render(request)
64	
65	    @app.get("/search", response_class=HTMLResponse)
66	    def search_page(request: Request, q: str = ""):
67	        return render(request, search=q, results=search_nights(diary.nights(), q))
68	
69	    @app.post("/nights")
70	    def add_night(
71	        request: Request,
72	        bedtime: str = Form(...),
73	        wake_time: str = Form(...),
74	        timezone: str = Form(...),
75	        notes: str = Form(""),
76	    ):
77	        try:
78	            diary.add_night(
79	                Night(
80	                    bedtime=local_input_to_aware(bedtime, timezone),
81	                    wake_time=local_input_to_aware(wake_time, timezone),
82	                    timezone=timezone,
83	                    notes=notes.strip(),
84	                )
85	            )
86	        except ValueError as error:
87	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=str(error))
88	        return RedirectResponse("/", status_code=303)
89	
90	    @app.post("/import")
91	    async def import_csv(request: Request, file: UploadFile):
92	        try:
93	            nights = parse_csv((await file.read()).decode("utf-8-sig"))
94	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
95	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=f"Import failed. {error}")
96	        count = diary.add_nights(nights)
97	        return RedirectResponse(f"/?imported={count}", status_code=303)
98	
99	    @app.post("/settings")
100	    def save_settings(
101	        request: Request,
102	        timezone: str = Form(...),
103	        quiet_start: str = Form(""),
104	        quiet_end: str = Form(""),
105	    ):
106	        try:
107	            diary.save_user(
108	                User(
109	                    name=diary.user().name,
110	                    timezone=timezone.strip(),
111	                    quiet_start=time.fromisoformat(quiet_start) if quiet_start else None,
112	                    quiet_end=time.fromisoformat(quiet_end) if quiet_end else None,
113	                )
114	            )
115	        except ValueError as error:
116	            return render(request, status_code=400, error=str(error))
117	        return RedirectResponse("/", status_code=303)
118	
119	    @app.post("/coach", response_class=HTMLResponse)
120	    def coach_page(request: Request, question: str = Form(...)):
121	        answer = ask_coach(coach, diary.nights(), question, trace_path)
122	        return render(request, question=question, answer=answer)
123	
124	    @app.get("/api/nudge")
125	    def api_nudge():
126	        nudge = next_nudge(diary.user(), diary.nights(), clock())
127	        if nudge is None:
128	            return {"nudge": None, "reason": "Log at least 7 nights to get a nudge."}
129	        return {
130	            "nudge": {
131	                "at": nudge.at.isoformat(),
132	                "local_time": f"{nudge.at:%H:%M}",
133	                "silent": nudge.silent,
134	                "text": nudge.text,
135	            }
136	        }
137	
138	    @app.get("/api/search")
139	    def api_search(q: str = ""):
140	        return {
141	            "query": q,
142	            "nights": [
143	                {
144	                    "id": night.id,
145	                    "night_of": night.night_of.isoformat(),
146	                    "bedtime": night.local_bedtime.isoformat(),
147	                    "wake_time": night.local_wake_time.isoformat(),
148	                    "timezone": night.timezone,
149	                    "notes": night.notes,
150	                }
151	                for night in search_nights(diary.nights(), q)
152	            ],
153	        }
154	
155	    @app.post("/api/coach")
156	    def api_coach(body: CoachQuestion):
157	        answer = ask_coach(coach, diary.nights(), body.question, trace_path)
158	        return {"answer": answer.text, "used_fallback": answer.used_fallback}
159	
160	    return app
161

"""Journal search: unit tests for matching and API/page tests."""

from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.search import matches
from nightjar.web import create_app


@pytest.fixture
def client(tmp_path):
    app = create_app(
        diary=Diary(tmp_path / "test.db"),
        coach=MockCoach(),
        clock=lambda: datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Toronto")),
        trace_path=tmp_path / "coach.jsonl",
    )
    return TestClient(app)


def add_note(client, day, notes):
    return client.post(
        "/nights",
        data={
            "bedtime": day + "T23:00",
            "wake_time": day + "T23:30",
            "timezone": "America/Toronto",
            "notes": notes,
        },
    )


def test_matches_exact_case_insensitive_and_typos():
    assert matches("Had Coffee late", "coffee")
    assert matches("Had coffee late", "cofee")
    assert matches("Had coffee late", "coffe late")
    assert not matches("Had coffee late", "tea")
    assert not matches("Had coffee late", "   ")


def test_short_words_need_exact_match():
    assert not matches("red light", "bed")


def test_search_api_tolerates_typos(client):
    add_note(client, "2026-03-10", "Had coffee late, restless")
    add_note(client, "2026-03-11", "Read a book, slept well")
    body = client.get("/api/search", params={"q": "cofee"}).json()
    assert body["query"] == "cofee"
    assert [n["notes"] for n in body["nights"]] == ["Had coffee late, restless"]
    assert client.get("/api/search", params={"q": "zzzz"}).json()["nights"] == []
    assert client.get("/api/search").json()["nights"] == []


def test_search_page_shows_search_text_escaped_and_results(client):
    add_note(client, "2026-03-10", "Had coffee late")
    page = client.get("/search", params={"q": "coffee"})
    assert "Results for: coffee" in page.text
    assert "Had coffee late" in page.text
    evil = client.get("/search", params={"q": "<script>x</script>"})
    assert "<script>x</script>" not in evil.text
    assert "<script>" in evil.text

"""End-to-end: a real browser adds the 7th night and the nudge appears.

Needs Chromium:  uv run playwright install chromium   (skipped if it's missing)
"""

import socket
import threading
import time
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest
import uvicorn
from builders import nights_at

from nightjar.coach import MockCoach
from nightjar.diary import Diary
from nightjar.web import create_app

pytestmark = pytest.mark.e2e
playwright_api = pytest.importorskip("playwright.sync_api")
NOON_IN_TORONTO = datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Toronto"))


@pytest.fixture
def base_url(tmp_path):
    diary = Diary(tmp_path / "e2e.db")
    diary.add_nights(nights_at("23:00", 6, first_night="2026-03-10"))  # one short of a nudge
    app = create_app(
        diary=diary,
        coach=MockCoach(),
        clock=lambda: NOON_IN_TORONTO,
        trace_path=tmp_path / "coach.jsonl",
    )
    with socket.socket() as sock:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = sock.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.05)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join(timeout=5)


@pytest.fixture
def page():
    with playwright_api.sync_playwright() as playwright:
        try:
            browser = playwright.chromium.launch()
        except playwright_api.Error as error:
            pytest.skip(f"Chromium not installed ({error.message.splitlines()[0]})")
        yield browser.new_page()
        browser.close()


def test_T_114_1_e2e_adding_the_seventh_night_shows_the_nudge(page, base_url):
    page.goto(base_url)
    expect = playwright_api.expect
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-cold-start")).to_contain_text("Log 1 more night")

    page.get_by_test_id("bedtime-input").fill("2026-03-16T23:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("wake-input").fill("2026-03-17T07:00")
    page.get_by_test_id("notes-input").fill("Read a book, lights out at 11.")
    page.get_by_test_id("add-night-submit").click()

    expect(page.get_by_test_id("diary-row")).to_have_count(7)
    expect(page.get_by_test_id("nudge-time")).to_have_text("22:15")

- **Tests:** I added one test for the log. I also pointed the test fixtures in `tests/test_search.py`, `tests/test_api.py` and the e2e test at a temp log, so test runs don't write into `logs/`.
